name: easyeda-pro-control
description: Safety-gated EasyEDA adapters, narrow symbol/PCB workflows and seven engineering skills.

interface.longDescription: Seven skills cover EasyEDA control, schematics, PCB layout, libraries, manufacturing, design review and extension development. Version-pinned typed API adapters distinguish public subsets, native equivalents, blocked implementations and concrete omissions. On the reviewed current runtime, supported observations include calculations, environment/editor metadata, PCB layers, loaded-view identities and bounded geometry. Attribute identity and value/placement reads retain ordered native component groups; they do not prove stored ownership. Attribute values are current model text, not necessarily raw formulas or rendered labels. Parentless String readers expose raw text and style, not rendered glyphs or font availability. Dimension geometry readers expose length/radius/angle tuples and line widths in mil. Their separate canvasUnit reflects the native current-canvas override, not verified annotation units or rendered measurements. Polygon Pad and component-pad readers expose bounded native path tokens in native-pad-style coordinates, not placed/rendered geometry or complete copper stacks. Offline discovery includes the result schema; populated live polygon validation remains pending. Image readers expose IDs and bounded vector/Picture placement and dimensions, not paths, binary assets, rendered bounds or complete canvas inventory. Project-only schematic metadata readers observe one or all containers or pages without opening editors. Selected pages require their expected parent, and both complete native maps are checked before selection; no circuit, saved-membership, worker-ownership or rename authority follows. Board metadata readers return UUID, raw title, zIndex and ticket from a complete bounded native map. Their selected native equivalent requires boardUuid instead of the public method's boardName; child relationships and public object parity are excluded. Installed143713 passed selected/all page reads and both board routes on a populated disposable fixture; later generations remain unvalidated. Fill/Polyline/Region serializers remain excluded because they can rebuild native children. Current writing is narrow: forward-only name/description edits for eligible unused project-local symbols, plus separate disposable symbol-copy and PCB-title workflows. Metadata/history prerequisites, original process ownership, full closed SQL effects and fresh saved readback remain mandatory. Historical disposable lifecycle successes do not admit another runtime or invocation. Ordinary PCB rename, referenced-symbol propagation, general schematic/PCB geometry and library writers remain disabled. Disposable schematic-container title rename has a registered original-owner forward lifecycle with aged SQL clocks, full stored effects, fresh saved metadata and child-roster verification. Installed143713 passed one complete disposable title-only lifecycle; the separate ordinary route and circuit editing are not enabled by that result. Explicit two-to-four-step phase batches retain individual acknowledgments and stop on pending observations or failure without retry. Installed163322 passed a separate batched disposable title lifecycle; historical cases do not admit another invocation. Passive SCH phase diagnostics report the current action/phase and elapsed monotonic time plus the last attempt's duration/outcome, including pending observations and asynchronous cleanup. They grant no writer-clock or replay authority; busy with nextPhase stopped is a reserved in-flight attempt, not terminal failure. PCB text Save and compiler-publication prerequisites do not enable writing. Checkpoint verification uses authorized artifact-local scratch and final receipt freshness checks. Status includes bounded admission-scan timings without caching authority. Historical admission reuses one private runtime descriptor owner within each scan while preserving fresh executable and evidence checks. Positional hashing avoids accumulating stream listeners. The ordinary-project schematic-title entrypoint seals target, startup, metadata peers and child projection before navigation and rechecks the closed baseline. Installed203733 passed this route's own title-only lifecycle on a disposable fixture, including full closed SQL, fresh metadata/peer/child-roster and both AST readback, final retained closure and unchanged SQL. Eligible ordinary-project container titles are now supported; sheet and circuit editing remain disabled. Legacy confirmDisposableProject:true is optional for old sealed journals, without granting current invocation authority. A separate validation-only native diagnostic tool now retains the original Windows process/Job and two anonymous pipes, with compiled installation pins, fixed browser/frame/script observations and cooperative closure. Caller IDs select retained observations, never ownership; no arbitrary debugger commands or code are accepted. Ordinary, replacement, scratch and status dispatch exclude unresolved diagnostic owners. Local inspection and original-owner cleanup do not require bridge authentication. Confirmed pre-creation refusal has a separate original-helper no-process cleanup proof; ambiguous creation and timeouts remain blocked. Existing-profile isolation, project-free startup, debugger-socket absence and connected diagnostic qualification remain unproved. Parent-scoped worker-only autoattachment can retain direct child sessions without pausing them. A selected worker requires exact source and context admission before one compiled side-effect-checked state sample; bounded flags, collection sizes and timer-presence markers expose no design content. A one-shot diagnostic-owned opener now binds an exact registered disposable file, managed checkpoint and empty source-qualified UI, acknowledging migrations, cache replay and automatic Save. It admits only the selected-project same-document transition; restored drawing frames, title drift and ambiguous outcomes remain refused and consumed. This worker-only opener does not create PCB-frame authority. A separate fixed model-state read requires an already source-qualified PCB frame and reaches compiler scopes without invoking Save or pausing. Bounded compiler counters, custom-footprint participants and dynamic-copper markers do not prove complete model membership, pending-producer completion, saved state or writer eligibility. Native creation now starts suspended, verifies the original image against retained file identities, then resumes once; post-create failure retains the process and cannot use no-process cleanup. The shared core passed a synthetic no-op Windows lifecycle, not connected EasyEDA qualification. General PCB writing remains unfinished. Failed native creation now retains its numeric Windows error and fixed error label through original-owner inspection and no-process cleanup; older evidence may lack that diagnostic. The facade can launch the existing EasyEDA profile, open a registered disposable project, retain its original process/Job and request normal closure. Opening may migrate data, replay caches, restore tabs and automatically Save. It is not isolated or guaranteed unchanged. Close acknowledgment is not termination or saved-state proof; prompts are never answered implicitly. Lost owners, ambiguous calls and incomplete journals retain their recovery gates. Offline schemas and coverage are not execution grants. Compiled topology and affected exports remain blocked for hidden annotation or Save All. The older tuple retains separately guarded readers, footprint typed API operations, native controls, checkpoints and recovery; the legacy writer is runtime-disabled. Arbitrary caller JavaScript, blind retries and unrestricted Save are unsupported. Missing installation files select offline-only startup. The historical reviewed tuple is connected-read-admitted; future mismatches fail closed within each capability profile. Historical validation cases are in a separate optional skill reference. Consult the packaged skills and generated per-method inventory for exact contracts, remaining work and scoped validation evidence.

Inspect the admitted EasyEDA project with exact readers and managed evidence.
Apply the requested typed design change and verify it after saving and reopening.
